A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StyleStudio. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and a 49-participant user study in Tables 1-2 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds style-similarity measurements, negative-style guidance analyses, and qualitative generation results.

M1.justification: Cross-modal AdaIN, teacher-guided early self-attention replacement, and Style-Based CFG retain the same procedures. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A unchanged. The explicit statement that replacement spans all UNet layers clarifies previously unspecified implementation scope rather than establishing a method revision.

E1.justification: The 52-prompt, 20-style benchmark and 30 color-object prompts remain unchanged. Selective-style-removal scenarios expand beyond v1's snow/ice and golden-leaf examples to nighttime and green-foliage conditions in v2 Figure 7 and wheat-field suppression in Figure 15.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains IP-Adapter, InstantStyle, CSGO, StyleAlign, StyleCrafter, StyleShot, and DEADiff. Figure 14 uses this same set. SCFG comparisons retain baseline, negative-text, and negative-style guidance; the newly cited Visual Style Prompt is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V2 Figure 14 adds CLIP and DINO style-similarity evaluation for two examples, and Figure 15 compares alternative negative-style images and CFG values 5-8. Existing benchmark settings, 1,000 generated images per method, and the 12-pair, 49-participant user-study protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 14 examines whether style-similarity metrics reward content leakage. Figure 15 adds sensitivity examples for negative-image selection and guidance strength. Existing component ablations, attention-map comparisons, teacher-timestep studies, and integration analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report fixed initial noise and random seed 42; this disclosure moves to Appendix A. Neither adds repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 retain their numerical results, including StyleStudio's 0.235 text alignment and 62.92%/50.85% user-study preferences. V2 adds per-example CLIP/DINO scores in Figure 14, SCFG outcomes in Figures 7 and 15, complex-prompt outputs in Figure 11, and additional gallery results.

T1.justification: Equations 1-7 retain the same mathematical content, and Algorithm 1 is relocated unchanged. Equation 7's explicit text/style superscripts clarify notation without changing its definition. No new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same three contributions and claims about prompt alignment, selective style control, layout stability, and integration without fine-tuning. Additional examples support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit limitations concerning teacher-model inference overhead and the expertise and manual effort required to generate negative-style images. Figure 14 also introduces the interpretation that CLIP/DINO style-similarity scores can favor semantic copying rather than faithful style transfer.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies replacement across all UNet layers. Original seed, inference-step, guidance-scale, hardware, and teacher-duration details remain available in Appendix A alongside the relocated pseudocode. The added layer specification improves documentation without demonstrating an implementation change.

R1.justification: V2 adds Visual Style Prompt and its self-attention swapping approach to related work. It also explicitly contrasts its attention replacement with prior editing methods' decoder-layer replacement. The remaining cited works and overall research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Related-work subsections are condensed into 'Stylized Image Generation,' several method and comparison passages are shortened, and Algorithm 1 and implementation settings move to Appendix A. 'More Results' and 'Limitations and Future Work' paragraphs are added while the overall section structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 substantially revises the visual presentation: separate method diagrams become a three-part overview with an SCFG schematic, the SCFG comparison is expanded and rearranged, and new metric and sensitivity panels appear. It also adds main-text galleries, redisplays existing bus examples, and reorganizes and expands the appendix galleries.

improvement.justification: V2 improves explanation through the consolidated method diagram and clearer implementation scope. The added SCFG sensitivity examples, metric-failure cases, and explicit practical limitations help readers assess the method. These are useful but limited gains: the main quantitative evidence is unchanged, and the new analyses remain small illustrative studies.
